headline: GAAP profit rebounds on LS Power deal; guidance reaffirmed
summary_short: NRG's Q2 2026 GAAP net income swung to $506M from a $104M loss a year ago on the LS Power asset acquisition and higher East capacity prices, while revenue rose 11% y/y to $7,481M but fell 27% sequentially from Q1's seasonal peak.
summary_long: Net income of $506M reversed a $104M year-ago loss, driven by the LS Power asset portfolio and higher realized East capacity prices, partly offset by milder weather and higher supply costs; non-cash hedge mark-to-market swung to a gain from a loss. Texas Adjusted EBITDA fell $131M y/y on mild weather and new-asset opex; East rose $370M on LS Power/CPower contribution and capacity prices, partly offset by Winter Storm Fern costs; Vivint rose $42M on customer growth. Adjusted EPS fell to $1.49 from $1.73 on acquisition-related interest expense, D&A, and share count. Cash fell to $162M, liquidity down $4.3B, funding the LS Power acquisition. NRG reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance unchanged across Adjusted Net Income, EPS, EBITDA, and FCFbG.

drivers.explanation: GAAP net income swung to a $506M profit from a $104M loss a year ago on the newly acquired LS Power portfolio and higher East capacity prices; NRG reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance unchanged.

Improvement was due to the addition of the LS Power portfolio and higher realized capacity prices in the East, partly offset by milder weather and higher supply costs, plus a swing to non-cash hedge gains from prior-year losses.
Y/y growth reflects contribution from the newly acquired LS Power generation assets and CPower, and higher capacity prices, partly offset by milder weather reducing retail load.
GAAP EPS swung positive on the LS Power contribution, but the company's own non-GAAP Adjusted EPS fell to $1.49 from $1.73, on higher acquisition-related interest expense, D&A, and share count.

Segment mix: Texas Adjusted EBITDA -$131M y/y on mild weather and new-generation opex; East +$370M on LS Power/CPower and capacity prices, partly offset by Winter Storm Fern costs; Vivint +$42M on customer growth.
Total liquidity fell $4.3B versus year-end 2025, "primarily driven by funding of the acquisition of generation assets and CPower from LS Power."
Y/y rise is explained by common stock issued as acquisition consideration: shares outstanding grew from 199.8M to 225.2M issued and additional paid-in-capital rose from $215M to $3,880M.
Y/y increase is consistent with $3,652M of new long-term debt proceeds drawn in H1 2026 (cash-flow statement), used alongside cash and equity to fund the LS Power acquisition.
